newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania needs better service for western tourists.
newsitem.headline: Romania needs better service for western tourists.

text.p: Romania cannot hope to attract tourists from Western countries until it upgrades facilities, the Balkan country's tourism minister said on Wednesday.
Akos Birtalan said Romania relied on tourists from poorer Moldova, Hungary, Ukraine and Bulgaria to bring in revenue.
Other tourists, he said, would continue to stay away until dilapidated roads were fixed, border crossings were simplified and tourist information made more easily available.
"Our target countries are mainly our neighbours in central and Eastern Europe, which make up the majority of tourists coming to Romania," he told a news conference.
"We cannot expect a spectacular rise in tourism from the West if we don't change the whole infrastructure."
Tourists coming to Romania often encounter potholed roads, poor service in hotels and a dearth of information on transport and attractions.

Tourism accounts for two percent of Romania's gross domestic product. Ministry statistics show some 58 percent of the 2.8 million foreigners who spent their holidays in Romania last year came from the four nearby countries.
The largest contingent of Western tourists came from Germany, 5.07 percent, followed by Italy with 2.45 percent.
Birtalan said his ministry planned to promote Romania to west Europeans or Americans as a point for completing tours of eastern Europe.
